Accelerated Bachelor’s and Master’s degrees (ABM) K. 1.0 Application and Admission.
Students applying for admission into ABM must do so through the URI Graduate School admission system.
Applicants must have earned at least 75 credits before they are eligible to apply.
Students will be enrolled in ABM after they have met all Graduate School admission requirements, and completed 90 undergraduate credits.
ABM students will be separately coded to distinguish them from other graduate students.
K. 1.1 Credit Requirements.
Only students accepted into the ABM program will be able to double count credits towards both the bachelor’s and master’s degrees.
The total number of credits that will be allowed to be double counted is up to one-third of the total credits required in the master’s program.
Only 500-level courses and 400-level courses designated for graduate credit are eligible to be double counted.
K. 1.2 Credits Taken Outside of a program or from another department.
Students can transfer credits between URI programs and departments.

Only credits earned at URI may be counted toward the master’s portion of the ABM.
K. 1.3 Time-to-degree Limit.
Students must complete all graduate degree requirements for an ABM within 2 years after their enrollment and coding as ABM students.
An additional year for programs with more than 30 credits may be allowed with the permission of the Graduate School.
Failure to complete the ABM in the allotted time effectively ends the ABM and students will not be able to double count credits.
K. 1.4 Program of Study.
ABM students must complete a Program of Study and submit it to the Graduate School in their first semester of enrollment in the graduate program.
The Program of Study lists the courses to be taken to fulfill the requirement of the master’s degree and those carried over from the undergraduate career.
If any changes in the original Program of Study are made, a new Program of Study must be submitted as soon as possible.
All ABM programs will have an established list of core courses and suitable electives that can be used to satisfy the requirements for the combined degree.
K. 1.5 Nomination for Graduation.

A Nomination for Graduation form must be submitted to the Graduate School by the ABM Program Coordinator in a student’s final semester.
Deadlines for submission are published in the Deadline Calendar on the Graduate School website.
The master’s degree will not be conferred on students prior to completion of their bachelor’s degree.
Simultaneous conferral of both degrees may be considered.
K. 1.6 Grades and Grade Point Averages.
Students must meet the acceptable grade requirements as described in Section 10 of the Graduate School Manual.
K. 1.7 Continuous Enrollment.
Continuous enrollment (see Section 4.40 of the Graduate School Manual) is required once students are coded and enrolled as ABM students.
K. 2.0 ABM Program Coordinators.
Every ABM shall have at least one Coordinator.
The Coordinator must assure that students enrolled in ABM are advised by the Coordinator or designated participating faculty.
Coordinators recommend approval or denial of applicant admissions to the Graduate School, approve Programs of Study, and submit Nominations for Graduation.

Coordinators and participating faculty also respond to programmatic questions from potential applicants, maintain files on active students, and keep records of the number of students who have participated in the ABM Program from its inception.

RATIONALE: There should be a demonstrable need for the program. B1. State the program objectives. This program prepares learners to execute the critical stages of identifying, planning, and evaluating learning in formal and informal environments applicable across a wide range of uses including corporate training, community education, and nonprofit programming. In today’s fast changing world where companies are hiring people to do work that did not exist when the employees were in college and communicating one’s mission and information clearly and successfully to a

broad audience are increasingly critical, many people are being thrust into education and training roles without the necessary understanding of their learners and how to create effective learning for them.
These learning professionals need to be able to diagnose learning needs, have a full range of learning methods and strategies to bring to bear on those needs, and the ability to evaluate its effectiveness.
Importantly this program focuses on more than the creation of learning.
It includes a focus on transferring the learning into action in their environments and program evaluation overall.

Session #1 Session #2 EDC 589: Foundations of Adult Learning and Development Learning and Development (L&D) Professionals need to thoroughly understand the multi-faceted adult learner to be effective learning designers, Instructors, program managers, and learning assessors.
This course examines the adult as learner with a strong emphasis on the factors at the foundation of adult learning and learning processes.
Participants will explore a range of theories and characteristics associated with adult learners.
Student Learning Outcomes Learners will: 1.
Identify factors that enhance learning and support for adult learners 2.
Explore the various theories and principles and apply them appropriately 3.
Discuss challenges to fostering adult learning and propose contextual solutions 4.

Develop a conceptual model of adult learning to be used as a tool for Learning Development EDC 590: Designing Learning Programs: Theory to Practice In this course key aspects related to the systematic design of learning programs for adult learners will be explored, namely (1) creating a needs analysis; (2) developing learning outcomes; (3) choosing appropriate methods for instruction and assessment; and (4) choosing effective learning formats.
You will develop your own learning design for an audience of your choice and present its four segments as a final project.

Develop learning objectives that are specific and measurable 3.
Choose appropriate methods of instruction based upon learning and development theories 4.
Select and apply assessment methods that align with learning objectives 5.

Summary description of proposed program (not to exceed 2 pages) The information age has brought advancements in technology and data collection techniques thatproduce an abundance of accessible data in all sectors. However, much of the ever-increasing data isunstructured and requires parsing for eﬀective decision making. Data Scientists make sense out of complex data or big data. Skills include: developing and applyingmethods to collect, record, store, analyze, and interpret data; eﬀectively extracting useful information;and detecting patterns, trends, and relationships in datasets for decision-making purposes. The data

scientist is often a storyteller presenting data insights to decision makers in a way that isunderstandable and applicable to their interests.
The ﬁeld of Data Science is interdisciplinary at its core, drawing knowledge from computer science,mathematics, statistics, and ethics, all within a framework of the domain area of the data itself.
Itsprimary goal is to gain insights and knowledge from any type of data, both structured andunstructured, and provide important resources to organizations that make data-driven decisions.Data Science is an exciting and dynamic ﬁeld that will continue to grow in importance to business,industry, science, many academic disciplines, healthcare, and government in the years ahead.
DataScientists are employed in all sectors, including ﬁnance, insurance, healthcare, social assistance, retailtrade, and manufacturing, both public and private.
Core expertise requirements for careers in data science are increasingly interdisciplinary and enabledby computational skills, requiring deep integration of data and domain subject knowledge to provideinnovative solutions to problems.

Students are exposed to an array of Data Science approachesenabling them to solve problems individually or as a part of teams.
Master of Science In Data Science Online Program Description Students learn to tackle problems that require core skills from computational, statistical, andmathematical sciences along with some domain area knowledge.
Emphasis is given tointerdisciplinary team building to solve problems that cannot be solved within a given discipline andto the ethical implications of data on individuals and society.
This program prepares data scientists toexcel in machine learning, analysis of large and/or unruly datasets, and visualization through anapproach that hones skills in problem solving and collaborative research.
In addition, studentsanalyze problems using advanced theoretical knowledge and skills of data science in statistics,machine learning theory, and mathematical methods to create innovative solutions to complexproblems in data science across a variety of domain areas.
This is a 10-course, fully online, asynchronous program that is oﬀered in the accelerated calendar ofsix 7-week sessions per year.

It is designed for working adults to take one course at a time, eachsession for 10 sessions.
Students can complete the program in 20 months.
Admission Requirements Students who complete the Online Graduate Certiﬁcate in Data Science will automatically beaccepted into the Online Master’s in Data Science.
For the Online Graduate Certiﬁcate in DataScience, the admission criteria is that prior courses in calculus, linear algebra, probability andstatistics, and programming in Python are recommended, but not required.
For the Online Master’s in Data Science, the requirement for admission is - prior coursework ordemonstrated equivalent experience in:a. programming in R and Python,b. calculus (similar to URI’s MTH 131 or MTH 141),c. linear algebra (similar to URI’s MTH 215), andd. introductory statistics (similar to URI’s STA 308 or STA 409). 2

This is a non-thesis program, requiring 30 credit hours and a culminating experience in the form of aproject and presentation that demonstrates the student’s ability to apply data science concepts tosolve a complex, relevant real-world problem. Aspects of the culminating experience are threadedthroughout the curriculum.
